in_plain_sight.title: In Plain Sight
in_plain_sight.subtitle: A well-oiled machine of a thriller.
in_plain_sight.series_note: Book Two in the Eve Tuant Series
in_plain_sight.synopsis: Following the devastating Greater Boston Massacre, CIA officer Eve Tuant returns—sharper, more guarded, and more single-minded than ever. The shift from chaos to the snake pit of Washington politics is seamless and treacherous. Backroom deals, carefully worded conversations, and the constant sense that someone is always listening. Three conspirators remain embedded at the highest levels of government. A looming assassination plot keeps the tension coiled tight. And when Eve realizes she has been marked for elimination, the paranoia ramps into overdrive. Smart, grounded, and relentlessly plotted — In Plain Sight is a high-stakes political thriller that doesn't let up.

reviews.author: RT Booksterr
reviews.title: Editorial Review
reviews.quote: A well-oiled machine of a thriller — smart but real, one that stays with you long after the last page.
reviews.full_text:
Richard DeVeau's IN PLAIN SIGHT draws you into a tense web of secrets, power moves, and survival — sparked by the brutal ripple effects of a devastating terrorist attack. The story begins at a comrade's funeral, where grief fuels a steely determination that takes hold of agent Eve Tuant from the start. Tuant isn't just another agent; she's been tested in war zones like Kabul and Kandahar. She possesses a unique mix of battlefield grit and brainpower — a cognitive science background that no training manual can teach.

The probe ramps up rapidly, shifting from the disaster's fallout to political intrigue. Eve starts chasing clues that link big-name insiders to the attack. At first, it feels like just another case, yet things get more serious when she ends up taking a bullet to the foot. The wound fuels her resolve.

Beyond the fast-paced scenes, the story shows Eve fighting inner battles. Her decisions weigh on her, making clear-cut answers hard to find. Her time in Afghanistan, especially memories with a close friend, contrast sharply with the cold game of power she finds herself in.

DeVeau delves into what justice means versus revenge, the fluid nature of trust, and a world where the lines between good and bad continuously blur. There are many memorable, well-written moments, blending raw detail with real people. That balance — part danger, part introspection — is what makes the pages keep turning.

reviews.author: Brian Emmet
reviews.title: More Eve Tuant? Yes, please!
reviews.quote: A roller-coaster plot, engaging characters, great local color and details — all packaged in a satisfying thriller and worthy successor to LIGHTS OUT!
reviews.full_text:
Eve Tuant — Canadian, special forces warrior, top-level intelligence operative, friend and advisor to POTUS, artist, gorgeous — what's not to like? In DeVeau's first book, LIGHTS OUT, Eve was key to unraveling the high-level conspiracy that caused the destruction of much of the Boston area and was aiming to do the same to D.C. In this sequel, that nefarious cabal is still at work, and it's Eve to the rescue.

Roller-coaster plot, engaging characters, great local color and details, with some reflections and ruminations on Big Questions, all packaged in a satisfying thriller and worthy successor to LIGHTS OUT!

reviews.author: Roger E. Breisch
reviews.title: A Very Satisfying Sequel!
reviews.quote: This book is great fun — read it and enjoy the twists and turns!
reviews.full_text:
I loved DeVeau's first book, Lights Out. I found it difficult to set down and said I couldn't wait for the sequel. I bought the sequel hoping not to be disappointed. I was just as enthralled with this volume as with the first. It was exciting how Richard thrust me into the continuing story of the protagonist, and kept me, once again, on the edge of my seat. In the first volume, the bad guys emerged throughout — even in the final pages. Even though you know the culprits early on in the sequel, it was a satisfying journey to finding justice! Now, I am anxious for the third installment!

This book is great fun — read it and enjoy the twists and turns!

reviews.author: Terri
reviews.title: An excellent sequel
reviews.quote: It required staying up late to finish it — couldn't put it down!
reviews.full_text: High stakes, political intrigue… an excellent sequel. When I got to the halfway point, I found it required staying up late to finish it — couldn't put it down! Looking forward to book three.

reviews.author: Bob Grenchik
reviews.title: Can't Wait for the Next One!
reviews.quote: I will be at a loss until the next one comes out!
reviews.full_text: Another good one by Richard DeVeau! Follows its predecessor, Lights Out, and continues the thrill. Takes you on an adventure to find out who and why someone would want to do so much destruction. A lot of time was spent getting every detail right. I don't read a lot of books, but always have to make time to read Richard DeVeau's work. Now that I've read both of them, I will be at a loss until the next one comes out!

reviews.author: Sneha
reviews.title: Loved it!
reviews.quote: High-stakes drama, political chaos, and a story that keeps you guessing 24/7.
reviews.full_text: If you're into high-stakes drama, political chaos, and stories that keep you guessing 24/7, this one's a solid pick. Just don't expect a calm reading experience — this book thrives on tension, and honestly? We love that.

reviews.author: Bill Blinstrub
reviews.title: In Plain Sight reveals those behind the attack
reviews.quote: Eve Tuant pulls at the many threads in this web of deception and intrigue until she reveals all those responsible.
reviews.full_text: I loved the follow-up to his excellent debut, Lights Out. DeVeau continues his tale with the fallout from the attack on Boston. Eve Tuant continues to pull at the many threads in this web of deception and intrigue until she reveals all those responsible. She then serves up justice in her own brutal, unforgiving style…

saffron_review.profile: reads.saffron on Instagram · 55.9K followers · Book collector since '93
saffron_review.text:
I thought I knew what kind of thriller this would be, but about twenty pages in I realized I was clearing my evening to finish it.

In Plain Sight picks up a year after the Greater Boston Massacre, and the weight of that event hangs over everything Eve Tuant does. She's sharper here, more guarded, and honestly more exhausted—and that made her feel real. The shift from the chaos of the first book into the snake pit of Washington politics was handled really well. I liked how the story leaned into backroom deals, carefully worded conversations, and the constant sense that someone is always listening. More than once I caught myself rereading a scene because I wasn't sure who was playing whom, which felt very intentional.

A couple things stood out. The idea that three conspirators are still embedded at the highest levels of government adds a steady undercurrent of dread, and the looming assassination plot keeps the tension tight without turning the book into nonstop action. There's also a stretch where Eve realizes she's been marked for elimination, and from that point on the paranoia ramps up fast—in a good way. It reminded me a bit of early Vince Flynn or Brad Meltzer, but with a more personal, grounded lead.

If I'm nitpicking, there were a few political maneuvering sections that slowed the pace just slightly. I didn't mind them, but readers looking for constant action might notice the dip. For me, the payoff was worth it.

I finished this yesterday and immediately wanted book three. If you like smart political thrillers, high-stakes conspiracies, and a capable female protagonist who doesn't feel invincible, I'd absolutely recommend In Plain Sight. It's a strong continuation and a step up in confidence from book one.

lights_out.synopsis: In Richard DeVeau's gripping debut novel, the serene landscapes of Door County, Wisconsin and the vast expanse of Lake Michigan become the opening scene in an explosive tale of deception, high-stakes political conspiracy, and domestic terrorism. With vivid prose and heart-pounding suspense, this is a masterfully woven thriller filled with intrigue, surprising plot twists, and compelling characters. Prepare to be grabbed by the collar from the first sentence and not released until the last period.
lights_out.synopsis_detail: A retired couple are murdered in their Wisconsin home—art and other valuables are stolen. A Lake Michigan oil tanker explodes and sinks that same night. Eve Tuant—special forces veteran, CIA officer, and leader of Boston's Homeland Security team—believes there is a connection between these two events. She and her team quickly find themselves in pursuit of a domestic terrorist—an MIT-educated, military trained missile genius with Ted Bundy-like psychopathy—to stop him before he carries out his next devastating attack. This one even more lethal than the overwhelming inferno he just unleashed on Greater Boston. As Eve closes in, she discovers these attacks are orchestrated by a US senator and a powerful cabal of highly placed leaders and lawmakers with a hidden agenda.

saffron_review.text:
Light's Out is a razor-sharp, adrenaline-fueled thriller that grabs you from its chilling opening scene and refuses to let go. Richard DeVeau delivers a gripping fusion of domestic terrorism, political corruption, and psychological intrigue—crafted with a pace and precision that fans of high-stakes thrillers will devour.

The novel opens with two seemingly unrelated catastrophes: a Wisconsin couple murdered in their home and an oil tanker exploding on Lake Michigan. Enter Eve Tuant—special forces veteran, CIA operative, and the formidable leader of Boston's Homeland Security team. Brilliant, relentless, and deeply human, Eve becomes the anchor of this electrifying story as she pieces together a pattern most would overlook.

Her target? A terrifying antagonist: an M.I.T.-trained missile expert with military polish and the cold, calculated cruelty of a serial killer. But the conspiracy runs deeper than one man. Eve soon uncovers a cabal of influential leaders, including a sitting U.S. senator, orchestrating a series of escalating attacks capable of devastating the nation.

Fast-paced, tightly plotted, and disturbingly plausible, Light's Out is a must-read for fans of political thrillers, military suspense, and heroes who fight in the shadows to protect a nation on the brink.

artist.statement: For me, painting is breathing... inhale ideas, ideologies and passions, exhale them onto canvas, paper, and wood. Exploring unusual materials and experimental techniques that create unique surface texture, line, form and color is an ongoing part of my process. I tend to work in a series manner, delving into a method or theme for a period of time, usually until it plays itself out. This can range from weeks to months, or sometimes years, before I move on to whatever is next. With each new series, I tend to bring along something from the work that preceded it. Over time, I've created my own visual vocabulary and voice.
